questions.question: A random variable $X$ follows a uniform distribution on $[2, 8]$. What is $P(X \le 5)$?
questions.explanation:
For a uniform distribution on $[a, b] = [2, 8]$:
$$f(x) = \frac{1}{b-a} = \frac{1}{8-2} = \frac{1}{6}$$

The probability is:
$$P(X \le 5) = \int_2^5 \frac{1}{6} \, dx = \frac{1}{6} \times (5 - 2) = \frac{3}{6} = \frac{1}{2} = 0.5$$

Geometrically, the interval $[2, 5]$ has length 3, and the total interval $[2, 8]$ has length 6, so the probability is the ratio: $3/6 = 1/2$.

questions.question: The time between customer arrivals at a store follows an exponential distribution with mean 10 minutes. What is the parameter $\lambda$ of this exponential distribution?
questions.explanation:
For an exponential distribution $\text{Exp}(\lambda)$, the mean is:
$$E[X] = \frac{1}{\lambda}$$

Given $E[X] = 10$ minutes:
$$10 = \frac{1}{\lambda}$$
$$\lambda = \frac{1}{10} = 0.1$$

The parameter $\lambda$ is the rate (events per unit time), so $\lambda = 0.1$ means one arrival every 10 minutes on average.

questions.question: A test score follows a normal distribution with mean 70 and standard deviation 10. What is the probability that a randomly selected student scores between 60 and 80?
questions.explanation:
Given $X \sim N(70, 10^2)$, we want $P(60 \le X \le 80)$.

**Standardize the bounds:**
$$Z_1 = \frac{60 - 70}{10} = -1$$
$$Z_2 = \frac{80 - 70}{10} = 1$$

So:
$$P(60 \le X \le 80) = P(-1 \le Z \le 1)$$

**Using the 68–95–99.7 rule:**
Approximately 68% of the data lies within $\mu \pm 1\sigma$ of the mean.

$$P(-1 \le Z \le 1) \approx 0.68$$

More precisely, using the standard normal CDF: $\Phi(1) - \Phi(-1) = 0.8413 - 0.1587 = 0.6826 \approx 0.68$.

questions.question: The lifetime (in years) of an electronic component follows an exponential distribution with $\lambda = 0.2$. What is the probability that the component lasts more than 5 years?
questions.explanation:
For an exponential distribution with $\lambda = 0.2$, the CDF is:
$$F(x) = 1 - e^{-\lambda x} = 1 - e^{-0.2x}$$

We want $P(X > 5)$, the probability that the component lasts more than 5 years:
$$P(X > 5) = 1 - F(5) = 1 - (1 - e^{-0.2 \times 5}) = e^{-1}$$

Alternatively, using the memoryless property and the complement:
$$P(X > 5) = 1 - P(X \le 5) = 1 - (1 - e^{-0.2 \times 5}) = e^{-1}$$

Note that $0.2 \times 5 = 1$, so the exponent is $-1$.

questions.question: A blood test result follows a normal distribution with mean 100 and standard deviation 15. If the normal range is defined as $[\mu - 2\sigma, \mu + 2\sigma]$, what percentage of test results fall outside the normal range?
questions.explanation:
Given $X \sim N(100, 15^2)$, the normal range is:
$$[\mu - 2\sigma, \mu + 2\sigma] = [100 - 30, 100 + 30] = [70, 130]$$

**Using the 68–95–99.7 rule:**
Approximately 95% of the data lies within $\mu \pm 2\sigma$.

Therefore, the percentage of results **outside** the normal range is:
$$100\% - 95\% = 5\%$$

More precisely, using the standard normal CDF:
$$P(X < 70 \text{ or } X > 130) = P(Z < -2) + P(Z > 2) = 2 \times (1 - \Phi(2))$$
$$= 2 \times (1 - 0.9772) = 2 \times 0.0228 = 0.0456 \approx 4.56\% \approx 5\%$$
